title: 1.1: States that when ZWJ emoji sequences exceed available space, the terminal wraps content across lines rather than keeping the sequence as a single unit
1.2: States that combining characters are stored in the cc_idx array of the CPUCell structure (e.g., up to 3 combining character indices)
1.3: States what reply the terminal generates to a control-sequence query that asks it to report part of its current state (for example a cursor position report or a DECRQSS reply)
1.4: States that kitty follows a display-oriented approach preserving exact codepoint sequences rather than strict NFC or NFD normalization
1.5: Reports runtime test output with actual cursor positions and cell widths (e.g., cursor x=8 for family emoji, cursor x=1 for VS15)
